chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-'Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them both), who said:
I asked him about a man who divorces his wife while he is absent. He said: 'His divorce is valid in all cases, and his wife observes the waiting period (iddah) from the day he divorces her.'

key_terms.عِدَّةٌ: waiting period (implied by context of تَعْتَدُّ)

ai.seo_question: Is a divorce valid if the husband is absent when he issues it?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies that a man's divorce pronounced while absent is legally binding (*sahih*) without requiring his physical presence or the wife's immediate knowledge, a key point in Shia jurisprudence regarding unilateral divorce. Consequently, the wife's waiting period (*iddah*) commences from the day the divorce is effectively communicated or takes legal effect, ensuring her rights to maintenance and remarriage are properly calculated. This ruling underscores the authority of the husband's declaration even in his absence, distinguishing it from conditional or revocable divorces that may require specific witnessing.
